chapter: Childhood in Tyler, Beaumont and Houston
title: First live jazz: his stepmother's touring show in Beaumont
summary: His father's new wife, a dancer in a travelling show, took him to see it, and the pit drummer with his big bass drum and tom-toms knocked him out.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Well, you haven't really -- now, you haven't really come to where you first heard a record.
When I first heard a record, --
When did you first hear jazz? What was your first time you heard some jazz?
That was in Beaumont, Texas.
Oh, you did?
Yes.
That would be, like, if you were 13, say about 1920.
Well, that was n't Louis that you heard then. Was it? Or was it the blues singers you heard?
No, it was -- like, my dad, he married again.
Yeah.
And this young lady he married happened to be in show business.
Yeah.
And she came into Beaumont, Texas, with this show. And she knew I was there, living in Beaumont. And she came by and picked me up and carried me to the show. She was dancing.
Your mother didn't like that, did she?
Well, I don't know whether she did, but she let me go.
She let you go.
Yes, because they were separated, anyway, so that really didn't matter.
Yeah, no.
They were good friends.
Oh, that's good.
And --
So you saw that show.
I saw the show. The had a drummer in there, playing the show, and that really knocked me out, too.
Yeah. It was flashy.
Well, yes, to me it was flashy, because he was playing the drums and --
Catching the steps and all.
The big bass drum with the Japanese tom toms on the side and all this. He played a solo.
He was in the pit?
He was playing for the -- he travelled with the show, too.
I mean, he wasn't -- yeah, he was in the pit.
And I just --
Did you see it from backstage or --
No, I was right there in front.
Yeah, yeah.
Since she was in the show, I could --
Yeah, sure. That was nice, yeah.
